SOAH DOCKET NO. 473-26-16349  |  PUC DOCKET NO. 59475
BEFORE THE STATE OFFICE OF ADMINISTRATIVE HEARINGS
JOINT APPLICATION OF ONCOR ELECTRIC DELIVERY COMPANY LLC AND LCRA TRANSMISSION SERVICES CORPORATION TO AMEND THEIR CERTIFICATES OF CONVENIENCE AND NECESSITY FOR THE BELL COUNTY EAST SWITCH TO BIG HILL SUBSTATION 765-KV TRANSMISSION LINE PROJECT
INTERVENOR AARON EDWARD HOWTON’S COMBINED REPLY TO APPLICANTS’ AND COMMISSION STAFF’S BRIEFS ON REMANDED PRELIMINARY ORDER ISSUE NOS. 11 AND 13
TO THE HONORABLE ADMINISTRATIVE LAW JUDGES:
Intervenor Aaron Edward Howton, appearing pro se, respectfully submits this combined reply to Applicants’ and Commission Staff’s briefs pursuant to SOAH Order No. 35, at 2–3 (Sept. 22, 2026) (PUC Item No. 6597), and SOAH Order No. 36, at 2 (Sept. 28, 2026) (PUC Item No. 6608). Order No. 35 expressly provides for responses on remanded Preliminary Order Issue Nos. 11 and 13 by October 19, 2026, and directs parties to use pinpoint record citations. Order No. 36 confirms that Order No. 35 in PUC Docket No. 59475 also applies to the related PUC Docket No. 59182; Order No. 35, rather than Order No. 36, establishes the response deadline. This reply addresses only Issues 11 and 13 and does not request reopening the evidentiary record. Applicants’ September 21, 2026 Directory of Evidence (PUC Item No. 6593) is treated as their early-filed brief under Order No. 35, at 2 n.3. Aaron responds to the Applicants’ positions and Commission Staff’s Initial Brief on Remand (PUC Item No. 6631) and respectfully asks the Administrative Law Judges to reaffirm their original recommendation to deny the application for a certificate of convenience and necessity in PUC Docket No. 59475.
I. SUMMARY OF REPLY
This reply asks the Administrative Law Judges to retain their previously recommended denial of the CCN application, based on the existing evidentiary record—not to revisit routing or introduce new evidence. The remand asks whether these particular proposed Import Path 2 facilities are necessary to meet a state or federal reliability standard (Issue 11), and what congestion savings may result from these facilities (Issue 13). Applicants and Commission Staff rely on systemwide planning results, but the cited briefs do not identify a facility-specific study removing Import Path 2 and quantifying the resulting reliability violation or the congestion savings attributable to restoring it. Staff Initial Brief at 2–4 (Item 6631); PFD at 180, Findings of Fact Nos. 128–129, as cited in Jason A. Howton Brief at 6 (Item 6630). The ALJs therefore have a record-supported basis to reaffirm their denial recommendation.
II. ISSUE NO. 11 — THE RECORD DOES NOT ESTABLISH PROJECT-SPECIFIC RELIABILITY NECESSITY
A. Applicants’ reliance on regional studies does not answer the remanded question. The Applicants’ Directory discusses NERC TPL-001-5.1, ERCOT planning criteria, the Permian Basin Reliability Plan (PBRP), the 2024 and 2025 Regional Transmission Plans, and Far West import constraints. Staff likewise invokes those studies. Staff Initial Brief at 2–3 (Item 6631). But a study showing systemwide violations and testing a plan with Import Path 2 already included does not show that a particular violation would persist without Import Path 2 or could not be corrected by another configuration. See PFD at 89 and Finding of Fact No. 130, cited in Jason Howton Brief at 5–6 (Item 6630).
B. Applicants’ own witness did not identify an isolated test. During cross-examination, Applicants’ witness Gurley testified he was not aware of a study isolating each line, because the lines were studied together. PFD at 88–89 (Aug. 20, 2026) (PUC Item No. 6441). He also treated an individual line’s necessity as an assumption flowing from a collective recommendation. PFD at 88–89, 180, FoF Nos. 128–129 (PUC Item No. 6441). It is therefore reasonable for the ALJs to conclude that the cited evidence supports planning for a network, but does not establish necessity of these facilities as a separate matter.
C. The study year and changing load assumptions matter. The PBRP evaluated its 765-kV import option at the 2038 load level, whereas for 2030 it evaluated a 345-kV import option. Applicants’ Ex. 1, Attachment 5 (PBRP), discussed in Jason Howton Brief at 7 (Item 6630). The PFD found a reduction of at least 3,571 MW from the PBRP non-oil-and-gas forecast under an adjusted forecasting method. PFD at 175, FoF No. 92, cited in Jason Howton Brief at 4 (Item 6630). These findings warrant a careful explanation why the same particular facilities remain necessary; Staff does not supply that counterfactual in its brief.
D. A federal planning standard does not itself command construction of this line. Federal law provides that an electric reliability standard does not include a requirement to enlarge facilities or construct new transmission capacity. 16 U.S.C. § 824o(a)(3). NERC TPL-001-5.1 informs required planning analyses and corrective actions; citing that standard is not identical to proving that certification of the specific Bell County East–Big Hill route is legally compelled. Under 16 TAC § 25.101(b)(3)(A)(ii), the economic-project criteria do not apply only if the proposed line is necessary to meet applicable reliability standards. While ERCOT’s recommendation receives great weight, the Commission still must evaluate need and substantiated forecast load. 16 TAC § 25.101(b)(3)(A)(ii)(II); Tex. Util. Code § 37.056(c), (c-1).
E. Staff’s conclusion does not cure the evidentiary gap. Staff cites its witness Poole and Applicants’ Directory and asserts that Import Path 2 is a reliability project. Staff Initial Brief at 2–3 & nn.3–7 (Item 6631). Aaron does not dispute the importance of reliability. He disputes the unsupported transition from “the combined statewide plan may resolve violations” to “these specific facilities are required.” The ALJs should explain precisely which admitted exhibit identifies an unmet standard absent Import Path 2, the relevant planning year and contingency, and why the record supports that identification. If no such record proof exists, Issue 11 should be answered in the negative as to the proposed facilities.
III. ISSUE NO. 13 — STATEWIDE SAVINGS DO NOT QUANTIFY SAVINGS FROM THESE FACILITIES
A. The Commission expressly remanded Issue 13. Staff takes the position that because the project meets the reliability classification, an economic-project savings analysis is unnecessary. Staff Initial Brief at 3 (Item 6631). That correctly describes the conditional exception in 16 TAC § 25.101(b)(3)(A)(ii), but it assumes the disputed answer to Issue 11. If facility-specific reliability necessity is not established, the project cannot avoid economic scrutiny merely by being called a reliability project. See Tex. Util. Code § 37.056(d); 16 TAC § 25.101(b)(3)(A)(i).
B. Staff’s 2034 and 2039 comparisons concern entire plans. Staff relies on ERCOT comparison figures for the 345-kV and 765-kV statewide plans, not a with/without-Import-Path-2 calculation. Staff Initial Brief at 4 & n.10 (Item 6631). In 2034 the cited consumer energy cost comparison shows $0.199 billion savings for the 345-kV plan and $0.063 billion savings for the 765-kV plan relative to the base case; in 2039 it shows $0.156 billion savings for the 765-kV plan, while the 345-kV alternative is above base-case costs. Id. Those figures may help compare plans, but they do not estimate the savings caused by this particular transmission project or establish its benefits against its costs.
C. Congestion rent is not an attribution study. Staff contends that lower plan-wide congestion rent will benefit consumers, citing Applicants’ evidence. Staff Initial Brief at 4 & nn.11–12 (Item 6631). Lower projected congestion rent in a whole-network model is not a quantified estimate of congestion cost savings attributable to the Bell County East–Big Hill line. The 2022 Commission rule expressly contemplates cost-benefit calculations attributable to the proposed project for an economic project. 16 TAC § 25.101(b)(3)(A)(i)(I)–(II).
D. Statutory consequences. Section 37.056(d) requires transmission-project criteria comparing estimated project costs for consumers with estimated congestion savings when a project is not necessary to meet state or federal reliability standards. If Issue 11 is answered no, the economic comparison becomes material. On this briefing record, Staff has not supplied a project-specific congestion-savings figure. The ALJs should answer Issue 13 by identifying this absence rather than treating the broad plan estimates as if they were attributable to Import Path 2. Tex. Util. Code § 37.056(d); Staff Initial Brief at 3–4 (Item 6631).
E. Existing record confirms that denial remains warranted. The evidence presented in the parties’ remand briefs does not resolve the deficiencies identified in the original Proposal for Decision. Applicants’ witness Gurley was unaware of a study isolating each line, and the ALJs observed that Applicants had not performed a partial-build study to justify Import Path 2 individually. PFD at 88–89, 180, Findings of Fact Nos. 128–129 (Aug. 20, 2026) (PUC Item No. 6441). The planning distinction also matters: the PBRP evaluated the 765-kV option at the 2038 load level, while its 2030 analysis considered a 345-kV import-path option. Applicants’ Ex. 1, Att. 5 (PBRP), as cited in Intervenor Jason A. Howton’s Brief at 7–8 (PUC Item No. 6630). Finally, Staff’s 2034 figures estimate savings of $199 million for the 345-kV plan versus $63 million for the 765-kV plan, but these are comparisons among broader plans, not the savings attributable to Import Path 2 alone. Commission Staff’s Initial Brief on Remand at 4 n.10 (PUC Item No. 6631). These record-based deficiencies support reaffirming the ALJs’ original recommendation to deny the CCN application.
IV. REQUESTED DISPOSITION
For those reasons, Aaron respectfully requests that the ALJs (1) answer Issue 11 by finding that Applicants have not shown these particular proposed Import Path 2 facilities necessary to meet a state or federal reliability standard; (2) answer Issue 13 by finding that the cited statewide-plan comparisons do not establish an estimated congestion cost savings attributable to these particular facilities; (3) preserve the PFD findings concerning the absence of an independent partial-build study, including Finding of Fact No. 128, rather than convert a general ERCOT planning recommendation into proof of individual project necessity; and (4) REAFFIRM THE PRIOR PROPOSAL FOR DECISION RECOMMENDING DENIAL of Applicants’ requested CCN amendments in Docket No. 59475. This reply requests no reopening of the evidentiary record and rests on the two remanded issues. See SOAH Order No. 35 at 2–3 (Item 6608); PFD at 88 (Item 6441), as cited in Jason A. Howton Brief at 6 (Item 6630).
Respectfully submitted,
/s/ Aaron Edward Howton
Aaron Edward Howton
Intervenor, Pro Se

Salado, Texas 76571
